target: AG1's claim that a federal Election Day holiday would remove work-based barriers for many voters, especially low-income workers.
objection: A federal holiday does not require private employers to give paid time off, so many low-income workers in retail and service jobs would still have to work and would not reliably gain voting access from the holiday.

target: AG1's claim that a holiday would broadly help low-income workers by making voting easier.
objection: Because the holiday would not reliably remove the main practical barriers for low-income voters, any turnout gains would be limited and uneven, leaving low-income workers disadvantaged relative to better-resourced voters.

target: AG1's assumption that a holiday automatically meaningfully increases turnout.
objection: Research indicates that an election holiday by itself is not an effective way to increase voter turnout compared with other voting-access reforms.

target: AG1's implication that a federal holiday is the best way to improve voting access.
objection: State-level laws requiring employer time off for voting and automatic voter registration are more direct and reliable ways to remove voting barriers than a national holiday.

target: AG1's claim that a national holiday would produce large benefits without much downside.
objection: Because a standalone holiday is likely to yield only limited gains, prioritizing it would consume political attention and resources and could slow or displace more effective reforms.

target: AG1's claim that a holiday would improve access for low-income workers.
objection: A holiday can disrupt school and child-care routines, forcing low-income households to find alternative supervision or rearrange work schedules, which can create extra time and cost burdens that interfere with voting.

target: AG1's claim that the holiday would not disadvantage low-income voters.
objection: Low-income households are less able to absorb disruptions to school and child-care routines, so those holiday-related burdens can fall more heavily on them and make voting harder rather than easier.
